normalized.governing_thought: Raise prices in 2027 for mid-market and enterprise only, and hold SMB prices while onboarding fixes the 2025 promotion cohort behind rising churn
executive_summary: Rising churn comes from the 2025 SMB promotion cohort, not from the customer base as a whole – SMB makes up 94% of the customers lost each month – Other SMB customers churn 2.1% a month, against 2.0% a year ago – 41% of promotion customers were active in month one, against 72% (p. 4–6)

Price is a real risk only in SMB, where Inkwell undercuts us; mid-market and enterprise can carry a rise – 52% of promotion churners cite price, against 18% of other churners – Our SMB win rate against Inkwell's $9 plan fell from 51% to 38% – A 10% mid-market price test left conversion unchanged (p. 8–10)
The CFO's 12% plan delivers less than it promises and puts its SMB gain at risk – Only $7.6M of the $10.3M can reach 2027 ARR – Its SMB gain is lost if half the promotion cohort leaves (p. 12, 13)

A targeted plan raises mid-market and enterprise prices, holds SMB and funds activation – With $4.2M from price, new customers must add only $0.8M – Activation could keep about $1M of promotion-cohort ARR in 2027 (p. 15–18)

slides.title: Churn is rising in SMB alone, which now accounts for 94% of the customers Palisade loses each month

evidence: Monthly logo churn H1 2025 → H1 2026: SMB 2.0% → 3.1%; Mid-market 0.6% → 0.8%; Enterprise 0.2% → 0.2%
94% of customers lost each month in H1 2026 were SMB customers (churn rate × customers)

claims.claim: SMB: the only segment where churn moved materially
Mid-market: a small rise on annual contracts that still grow in value
Enterprise: unchanged, held in place by multi-year contracts
Board dashboard: one undefined, blended rate hides this mix; report churn by segment

slides.title: The 2025 promotion cohort, not the core SMB base, is behind the rise in churn

claims.claim: Other SMB: almost unchanged in a year, despite Inkwell's October 2025 launch

claims.claim: The break-even ignores other SMB customers; any reaction from them makes the margin smaller

slides.title: Four moves turn the CFO's increase into a targeted plan that protects SMB while it recovers

claims.claim: Raise mid-market list prices 10% at renewal
evidence: 10% rise tested on new sign-ups in 2024, conversion unchanged

claims.claim: Raise enterprise prices up to the cap at 2027 renewals
evidence: 7% cap on yearly rises for 60% of enterprise ARR

claims.claim: Hold SMB list prices and activate the 2,100 promotion customers
evidence: 41% of promotion customers active in month one, against 72%

claims.claim: Test an SMB rise on new sign-ups before a Q3 decision
evidence: 38% SMB win rate against Inkwell, which the test must protect

claims.claim: Decision for December: raise prices for mid-market and enterprise only, worth about $4.2M of 2027 ARR
evidence: The targeted plan forgoes about $3.4M of the CFO plan's realistic $7.6M, most of it the SMB rise at risk

slides.title: With today's retention, the targeted plan leaves new customers only $0.8M of ARR to add to reach the 2027 goal

claims.claim: With today's retention, the targeted plan leaves new customers only $0.8M of ARR to add to reach the 2027 goal
evidence: ARR bridge: ARR mid-2026 $86M; Existing base at today's NRR +$7.98M; Mid-market +10% +$3.485M; Enterprise up to 7% +$0.672M; New customers needed +$0.763M; 2027 goal (+15%) $98.9M
$12.9M growth goal (15% × $86.0M) − $7.98M base at today's NRR − $3.5M mid-market +10% − $0.7M enterprise +7% = $0.8M left for new customers

claims.claim: 32% of the growth the goal needs comes from the two targeted price moves
Existing base: mid-market and enterprise growth outweighs SMB losses
New customers: a remainder activation could cover
Check that the 2027 new-customer plan clears $0.8M of ARR

slides.title: Activation could keep about $1M of promotion-cohort ARR in 2027, on a realistic target rather than halved churn

claims.claim: Activation could keep about $1M of promotion-cohort ARR in 2027
evidence: $3.4M left after 12 months if the cohort churns 2.1% a month, like other SMB customers
− $2.4M left after 12 months at its implied 4.9% a month today
= $1M of ARR kept by bringing the cohort to the SMB norm
Starting point: $4.4M of ARR at full price; 12-month survival = (1 − monthly churn)^12

claims.claim: We plan on the SMB norm, not on the promise to halve churn
evidence: Customer Success expects to halve SMB churn to 1.55%, below the 2.0% SMB had before the promotion
Target instead: promotion churn falls to 2.1% from January 2027 and stays flat for the year

claims.claim: The cohort's churn may already be easing, as most leavers went soon after the discount ended

evidence: Dec 2026: Leadership decision; Q3 2027: SMB price gate
Mid-market +10%: New prices at each renewal
Enterprise up to 7%: Notices per contract terms
SMB activation: Onboarding for the promotion cohort; Extend to all new SMB sign-ups
SMB price test: New sign-ups only; Decide for existing SMB
Churn reporting: Segment churn on the board dashboard

claims.claim: Gate for an SMB rise: promotion churn near 2.1%, and no further fall in the 38% win rate against Inkwell

normalized.recommendation: Raise prices in 2027 for mid-market and enterprise only, and hold SMB prices while onboarding fixes the 2025 promotion cohort behind rising churn. Four moves: raise mid-market list prices 10% at renewal; raise enterprise prices up to the cap at 2027 renewals; hold SMB list prices and activate the 2,100 promotion customers; test an SMB rise on new sign-ups before a Q3 decision. Decision for December: raise prices for mid-market and enterprise only, worth about $4.2M of 2027 ARR.

alternatives_considered.option: CFO's 12% list-price rise on every plan
alternatives_considered.treatment: Rejected: "delivers less than it promises and puts its SMB gain at risk" — only $7.6M of the $10.3M can reach 2027 ARR once renewal dates and enterprise caps are applied; its SMB gain ($2.5M) is wiped out if about half (51%) of the promotion cohort leaves because of the rise. The targeted plan forgoes about $3.4M of the CFO plan's realistic $7.6M, most of it the SMB rise at risk.

Deferred: hold SMB list price; test an SMB rise on new sign-ups before a Q3 decision, gated on promotion churn near 2.1% and no further fall in the 38% win rate against Inkwell. A 12% rise would put the SMB plan at $16.80, 87% above Inkwell's Starter plan.

alternatives_considered.option: Customer Success target to halve SMB churn to 1.55%
alternatives_considered.treatment: Not used for planning: "We plan on the SMB norm, not on the promise to halve churn"; target instead is promotion churn falling to 2.1% from January 2027.

assumptions_and_uncertainties: Customer counts are mid-2026. The board dashboard's "1.4% → 2.3%" is not defined and does not match these segment rates
Promotion-cohort churn is implied: (5,900 SMB customers × 3.1% − 3,800 other SMB customers × 2.1%) ÷ 2,100, using mid-2026 counts
Exit-survey response rates are not in the briefing pack
The 2024 test covered new sign-ups only; existing customers may react more at renewal
Caps assumed to cover 60% of renewing enterprise ARR, as of all enterprise ARR
Break-even: customers who leave would otherwise have paid today's price; all SMB ARR renews in 2027
The break-even ignores other SMB customers; any reaction from them makes the margin smaller
ARR bridge assumes each segment keeps its trailing 12-month retention; 2027 new-customer bookings are not in the briefing pack
Activation target: promotion churn falls to 2.1% from January 2027 and stays flat for the year; the cohort's churn may already be easing
Fictional company; synthetic data from the briefing pack

normalized.extraction_notes: The deck came as plain text, so there were no images to view. I copied chart values from the [Chart] data series and wrote them as percentages and dollar amounts (for example, 0.049095 is shown as 4.9%). On the waterfall charts (slides 12 and 16), I left out the 'base' series because it only positions the bars, and reported the 'ARR added'/'ARR' values. On slides 6, 13, 16 and 17, the numbers and labels are separate text fragments; I paired each number with its label by their order in the text. On slide 18, the quarter each Gantt bar falls in can't be read from the text, except for the labels that name a time. The executive-summary entries join each point with its sub-bullets and page references.
